cards.card: Visa Platinum US Dollar Credit Card
Visa Infinite US Dollar Credit Card

note: Nigeria's large card issuers were tried: Stanbic IBTC, Access Bank and Zenith Bank (Access and Zenith are among the largest banks by assets; Stanbic IBTC is the best-known naira credit card issuer). Stanbic IBTC Bank's page for its Visa Platinum Naira credit card (read 30 October 2026): interest of 3% a month, a new card fee of N1,075, a management fee of 1% of the limit at issuance, renewal and each limit increase (written at issue and at a raise; renewal isn't written, as the page doesn't say how often it falls), and up to 55 days interest free. Its other credit cards' pages couldn't be found from the bank's listing, which loads them by script; its 2023 pricing guide, the latest the bank serves, gives 2.5% a month and is older than the card page, so isn't used. Access Bank's rates guide gives its personal credit cards (naira Classic; dollar Black, Platinum, American Express Gold and Platinum) joining, maintenance, late, cash advance and conversion fees and an interest rate of '2.5% on outstanding balance' without the period it's charged by, so they aren't written; Access's American Express page, which a search showed stating a monthly rate, answered 504 three times. Zenith Bank Nigeria publishes no card tariff that could be found. On 30 October 2026 Stanbic IBTC's credit card listing was rendered (it loads its cards by script) and each of its personal cards' own pages read, adding its six other credit cards: the Visa Silver, Gold and Infinite Naira cards (3% a month, N1,075 for a new card, up to 55 days interest free; the Gold's and Infinite's management fee of 1% of the limit at issuance and each limit increase is written as the Platinum's is, while the Silver's page charges its 1% at issuance and increase without saying 1% of what, so it isn't written) and the Visa Gold Dollar, Platinum US Dollar and Infinite US Dollar cards, denominated in US dollars (2.5% a month, up to 55 days interest free; the Gold Dollar's and Platinum's annual maintenance fee of $10.75 is written; the Infinite's $10.75 maintenance fee states no period, so it isn't written and the card says its fees to hold it aren't published; the Gold Dollar's and Infinite's 1% of the limit is written at issue and at a raise, the Platinum's states no base; the N1,075 issue fee on the dollar cards is charged in naira, which a dollar card's terms can't carry, so it isn't written). The Gold page also carries an older costing table (2.5% a month, N3,150 a year, N2,000 late, 1% of the limit twice yearly) that its own headline terms (3% monthly) contradict and that matches the 2023 pricing guide, so the headline terms are written. The 'penal fee' of 1% of the overdue limit on the Silver and Platinum USD names no base the game holds and isn't written; VAT is added to some fees without its rate, so no tax is written. The Zero Limit Gold USD card works as a prepaid card and isn't written. Wave 4 (30 October 2026), for a second and third bank: UBA's and FCMB's card pages answered an Incapsula bot check, Zenith's an Incapsula 403, GTBank's credit card page redirected away with no content, First Bank's didn't answer, Fidelity's answered a Cloudflare 404 and Ecobank Nigeria's a captcha; a web search for any of these banks' naira card rates found only Stanbic IBTC's pages and the Central Bank's guide to charges. So Stanbic IBTC stays the only bank written. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: No minimum payment is published for Stanbic IBTC's seven cards; tried: its card list and each card's page (read for wave 4 and searched again 2026-10-30: up to 55 days interest free and repayments through internet banking, no share), the Central Bank of Nigeria's guide to charges (the 2020 edition's address answered 404; a search found no rule on a minimum), a search in English (only Stanbic Kenya's 10%, another bank), and archive.org's API (a snapshot of the card list of 8 September 2026; web.archive.org itself is refused by this research's connection).
